incident-bot: Pager duty alert triggered: smart-routing policy (rollout=canary-v2) observed >20% 5xx over 5m, sticky fallback engaged, region failover loops detected :rotating_light:
Alex Cheung: paging — I'm on call, looking now. what's the impact?
incident-bot: Affected route: /v1/generate (customer tier: hosted). ~12% of requests currently hitting sticky fallback variant (canary->stable oscillation). Errors: 5xx spike (502/504), latency spike to 1.8s p50 -> 3.2s p50 on fallback.
Marta Ruiz: I'm in. can we pause the rollout? status of canary instances?
Nate: canary-v2 has degraded memory pressure on region eu-west-1, some nodes OOM-killed, autoscaler retrying. Logs show kv-cache miss storms when model switching happens.
Alex Cheung: quick mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout 2) disable sticky fallback for the route 3) if needed, rollback canary to v1. Need handoff to infra to drain problematic nodes.
Marta Ruiz: agree. pausing rollout now via console.
Marta Ruiz: ```
# API call to pause rollout
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/12345/pause" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
deploy-bot: Rollout 12345 status: PAUSE_REQUESTED -> PAUSED (by marta) :white_check_mark:
Alex Cheung: disabling sticky fallback for that policy to prevent oscillation. Nate, can you apply a temporary policy override?
Nate: applying override. ```
# policy override
PATCH /policies/route-6789
{ "fallback": { "strategy": "random-variant", "sticky": false } }
```
Nate: override applied. propagation ~30s.
support-bot: customer-impact note: 18 customer sessions reported increased latency, 4 internal error escalations opened. tagging affected accounts for SRE follow-up.
Alex Cheung: monitoring for 10m. if error rate drops <2% we'll keep paused and proceed to safe rollout. if not, we'll rollback.
Marta Ruiz: I'm seeing 5xxs drop to 4.5% and tail latency improving. Sticky fallback count trending down. Good sign.
Samir Patel: heads-up — region routing metrics show a hiccup in us-central-1 too, but lower severity. could be cascading when stable variant receives extra load. recommend throttling canary traffic away from us-central-1.
Nate: throttling applied: ```
# route weight adjust
POST /routing/weights
{ "canary-v2": 0.0, "stable-v1": 1.0, "region": "us-central-1" }
```
Alex Cheung: that's aggressive but fine for now. We avoid cross-region loops.
Marta Ruiz: infra will cordon the bad nodes in eu-west-1 and spin replacement nodes. Nate, coordinate with infra to drain before autoscaler tears down.
Nate: on it, cordon+drain started. ETA ~7m.
deploy-bot: Rollout 12345 -> PAUSED, Traffic reweighted to stable-v1 in us-central-1, policy override active.
Alex Cheung: customer impact summary for pager: initial spike affected ~0.8% of total requests for hosted customers for ~12 minutes, peaked errors at 22% for the route. No data exfiltration. Notifying support to reach out to impacted customers.
support-bot: support notifications queued. template used: "We observed elevated errors for some requests earlier today; we've mitigated and paused a canary rollout. We're following up with a detailed RCA."
Marta Ruiz: decision point — keep paused and re-run canary with capacity adjustments & kv-cache warming, or rollback to v1? Thoughts?
Samir Patel: prefer rollback first to stabilize for customers, then reattempt canary behind feature-flag and with cache prewarm.
Alex Cheung: agree. initiate rollback. Marta, can you trigger rollback?
Marta Ruiz: initiating rollback now. ```
# rollback
POST /rollouts/12345/rollback -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
deploy-bot: Rollback started -> Rollback completed (canary removed, stable-v1 serving). :white_check_mark:
Nate: cordon/drain finished. new stable capacity holding. latency back to baseline.
Alex Cheung: monitoring indicates error rate back to <0.5% and latency within SLO. closing pager but keeping thread open for notes.
incident-bot: Incident recorded: INC-2026-0427-01. severity: SEV2. duration: 00:21:35. root cause: canary variant memory pressure + sticky fallback policy created oscillation under partial node failure.
Marta Ruiz: postmortem actions (short): 1) add canary capacity safety check and prewarm kv-cache, 2) make sticky fallback opt-in per-route and add circuit-breaker, 3) autoscaler backoff adjustments to avoid simultaneous restarts.
Alex Cheung: assigning follow-ups: Marta (canary safety), Nate (policy toggle UX and overrides), Samir (runbook update for sticky fallback), Support (customer comms).
Samir Patel: taking runbook task. will add explicit handoff checklist for rollouts + emergency rollback commands.
Alex Cheung: handoff to next on-call Samir. Samir, you're primary for any post-incident follow-ups.
Samir Patel: taking it. thanks team. :thumbsup:
Marta Ruiz: thanks everyone. will write up initial RCA and link here when ready.
Alex Cheung: closing thread in 2h unless follow-ups.
